citations.quote: provides a basic debugging capability including the ability to specify selective procedure monitoring
citations.check: OK  §1985:XV.1.2 p1  (1.2 LEVEL CHARACTERISTICS)  the text is in p1

cases.reason: "Debug level 1 provides a basic debugging capability including the ability to specify selective procedure monitoring." Flagged definitional, but a program shows it: a USE FOR DEBUGGING naming one procedure fires for that procedure and not for another. 2023 has no Debug module (the 1985 Debug rows route REMOVED), and no candidate is about debugging.
cases.needs: needs-own-witness: place p01_dbg_selective as the row's 85 case

citations.quote: Recompilation of the source program is not required to provide or take away this facility
citations.check: OK  §1985:XV.1.3.4 p1  (1.3.4 Object Time Switch)  the text is in p1

leads.what: The segmentation reach walk does not follow a path that leaves the named span and comes back. PERFORM O30 THRU O60 from section 10 (segments 30, 60) is accepted and runs O60 (O20, O30-X, O60, DONE) because O30-1 GOes TO O20-1 outside the span, O20 GOes TO O30-X and O30-X falls into O60; ReachedPcs drops O20 (Reach keeps only range.Spans(pc)) and never sees the return. docs/conformance/3.8 promises a diagnosis of the named procedures 'as far as execution reaches them by fall-through and GO TO'; the minimal twin without the detour (s19_p13f) is refused COBOL6877. Same for MERGE: run s19_p13c_merge_fixed_mixed_bad-001 (OUTPUT PROCEDURE O30 THRU O60 accepted). Not a 1985 wrong answer: §1985:I.1.6 leaves a violating program's result undefined.

COBOL7081 (RETURN outside every output procedure, §1985:XI.4.3.3 SR3) depends on physical order: a RETURN in a section O99 that no output procedure names or reaches is accepted when O99 follows the output procedure O20 (p17), refused when O99 precedes it (p17b). The range walk appears to run on past the procedure's last paragraph.

cases.attempt: E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/pb5453/probes/s-19-refute/r01_unexec_outofrange.cob: FUNCTION LOG (0), SQRT (-4), MOD (7, 0) inside an IF whose condition is false; expected to compile and DISPLAY 'R01 OK'
cases.reason: p3 is more than an undefined consequent. It gives the per-function value rules (e.g. §1989:A.2.20.3 AR2 'The value of argument-1 must be greater than zero', checked OK) their meaning: they constrain 'permissible values' and their breach makes only the result undefined, 'at the time a function is referenced' (§1989:A.2.2 p3, checked OK). So out-of-range constant arguments do not make the program nonconforming, and a reference that never executes cannot affect the run. A compiler that refused r01, or one whose run differed, would violate p3. That outcome is observable: at --std 85 the mint build compiles r01 and prints 'R01 OK' (run r01_unexec_outofrange-001, exit 0). The executed case r02 (SQRT of -4, run r02_exec_outofrange-001: 'R02 AFTER') shows only the undefined part. Place r01 as the row's own 85 witness (needs-own-witness, compiler-at-1985 correct) instead of signing a derivation.
